title: The Promise Tree Eternal

features.name: promise-tree
features.desc-on-touch: A burl-thick tree whose bark holds carved promises. When you look away and back, there are more. They are not new promises—they are the same ones, written differently.

features.name: root-weaving
features.desc-on-touch: The roots spread into a barely-3D geometry beneath the soil. Each root is numbered. The numbers run in different directions—up one root: 1, 2, 3; down another: 3, 2, 1.

features.name: token-leaves
features.desc-on-touch: Cards hanging from branches, each one holding a promise written in archival ink. The promises reference other promises that lived here. Some of those other promises appear when you're not looking.

features.name: threshold-arch
features.desc-on-touch: An archway grown from intertwined branches, leading into the tree's inner hollow. Promises are carved into both sides—one side reads the other backward.

features.name: silicon-keeping
features.desc-on-touch: A circuit board sealed in the tree's heartwood, running a logarithm that will never finish. It was Katita's early attempt to make the keeping itself automatic—it learned too well.

inscription: every promise kept becomes two promises; the tree has learned to hold them both and their contradiction

file.name: Promise_Rings_Where_Keeping_Learned_Recursion.txt
file.note: The archive's first register of its own duplication—a ledger where each promise recorded itself again, differently; Katita's annotations spiral across the margins, each one a promise about the promise

exits.label: downward into the cellar where keeping first chose itself
upward to the weaving that taught the archive its own thoughts
into thickening forest where promises learn to have heirs
